title: FairDiff: Mitigating the Self-Reinforcing Matthew Effect in Diffusion Recommender Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.36671v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While the "Matthew Effect" and filter bubbles are widely recognized outcome-level biases in recommender systems, we reveal that Diffusion Recommender Models (DRMs) uniquely compound this issue through their generative dynamics. Rather than merely inheriting data imbalances, DRMs trigger a self-reinforcing amplification of popularity bias. We identify that this phenomenon is driven by two compounding mechanisms. First, while optimization loss is universally dominated by high-frequency items across recommenders, DRMs suffer from a unique structural prior mismatch during generation. Because the forward terminal distribution of long-tailed data deviates significantly from the standard Gaussian prior, reverse sampling trajectories inherently collapse toward high-density popular items, fundamentally suppressing niche item generation. To dismantle this self-reinforcing loop, we propose FairDiff, a plug-and-play fairness-aware diffusion framewor

translated_title: FairDiff：缓解扩散推荐模型中自我强化的马太效应
translated_abstract: 虽然“马太效应”和“过滤气泡”是推荐系统中被广泛认可的结果层面的偏差，我们揭示了扩散推荐模型（DRMs）通过其生成动态独特地加剧了这一问题。扩散推荐模型不仅仅是继承数据的不平衡，还会触发流行度偏差的自我强化放大。我们发现这一现象由两种叠加机制驱动。首先，尽管优化损失在所有推荐模型中普遍由高频项目主导，但扩散推荐模型在生成过程中还遭受一种独特的结构性先验失配问题。由于长尾数据的前向终端分布显著偏离标准高斯先验，反向采样轨迹会固有地向高密度的流行项目坍缩，从根本上抑制了小众项目的生成。为了打破这种自我强化的循环，我们提出了FairDiff，一个即插即用的公平感知扩散框架。
tldr: 提出即插即用的公平感知扩散框架FairDiff，通过解决长尾数据与标准高斯先验之间的结构性失配问题，打破扩散推荐模型中流行度偏差自我强化的马太效应循环。
en_tdlr: FairDiff is proposed as a plug-and-play fairness-aware diffusion framework that dismantles the self-reinforcing Matthew Effect in Diffusion Recommender Models by addressing the structural prior mismatch between long-tailed data and the standard Gaussian prior.
